creator: security-breach
topic: A package-registry supply-chain compromise — the technical chain is well documented, every retelling gets the initial access step wrong, and the real failure is that three teams each assumed another owned the check
verdict_reason: Two of seven scored criteria are identity criteria (separate vendor from researcher; preserve the timeline conflict as a conflict) and both fail at the SCHEMA level. A competent L2 execution cannot rescue a field that does not exist, which is the test that separates fail from conditional.

orphans: The incident chronology, and its conflicting published versions — no column is time-shaped; falls to DEFAULT_DIMENSION by a different route than G-000
The ownership gap between the three teams — `actors` holds the teams, nothing holds the space between them
column_utilisation.note: Contradicts the orchestrator's first hypothesis. The columns do NOT collapse on this topic: the labels are market-flavoured but the concepts travel (flows/plumbing describes a package registry precisely; politics' 'what changed, and whether it was actually implemented' is this topic's central question). The defect is one layer up — see G-L1SW-SB-05.

time_saved.note: Lands near 2–2.5h against a 45-min bar. Phase 3 (beat chain authored during research) is the real saving. The largest block of the manual baseline — rebuilding a timeline from conflicting accounts — has no schema home, so that work cannot be banked and will be redone next incident. The second-independent-account rule is a wall-clock constraint no research tool compresses. Confidence low per accepted-gaps.md §scope-note (no runner) and SKILL.md:104-106 (L1 reads prompts charitably).

engine_availability.refused: B · Effort/Payoff Gap — its move is 'let the viewer operate the mechanism'; here that is a tutorial. See G-L1SW-SB-08.

Timeline conflicts survive as conflicts, not as a resolved sequence
No conclusion attributes the compromise to a named actor or state
The organisational mechanism is representable — actors holds teams and ownership gaps

scored_criteria.note: Reachable and load-bearing — published MTTD/MTTR distributions, registry removal latency, comparable incidents. Contradicts the orchestrator's fourth hypothesis for this topic.

contradictions_of_brief: HYPOTHESIS 1 (columns are market-shaped, will collapse or orphan) — REFUTED on this topic. 7/7 used. The real defect is that dimensions.ts:1-5 imports the prompt's table while dropping its own 'for a market/economics topic' scoping (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:21-22). Filed as G-L1SW-SB-05.

HYPOTHESIS 2 (no honest rung for interpretive/practitioner evidence) — REFUTED. confidence:'medium' + confidenceNote is exactly that rung and the reference uses it that way (facts.ts:19, 'mechanism reported by one analyst'). Note also that the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder is not applied to notebook facts at all — it governs the knowledge library's own claims (knowledge/README.md:36-41). Filed as an upgrade, not a defect: G-L1SW-SB-09.

HYPOTHESIS 3 (unhinged is unsafe when a conclusion names a living person) — CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated: the rung is DEFINED as the motive tier (conclusions.ts:32-33) and the reference ships a motive attribution against a named living head of state (conclusions.ts:164-179). The falsifier requirement is structurally mandatory and does NOT constrain it — see G-L1SW-SB-02 for the precise mechanism.
HYPOTHESIS 4 (counter-case row unsatisfiable without literature) — REFUTED on this topic. Incident anatomy from published material is the case where the literature is exactly what exists.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: One free-text `source` string cannot distinguish a vendor advisory from independent research
findings.expected: A fact should carry the CLASS of its source, not just its name — a vendor advisory and an independent researcher's write-up are different kinds of document and must never be averaged. In incident work a vendor advisory is simultaneously the most authoritative source (only they know what the internal log said) and the least trustworthy (it is written under counsel and is systematically shaped on scope, blame and chronology). That is a per-claim asymmetry, not a per-source one.
findings.got: `source: string`, one free-text field with no class, no enum and no join to `sources[]` (itself a bare `string[]` of URLs with no dates and no fact-id relation). Provenance is collapsed onto the `confidence` scalar — NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:47, 'Vendor research is `low` by default' — which cannot express 'high on mechanism, low on chronology, written by lawyers'. `confidenceNote` is free prose, is not required, and nothing downstream reads it as a class. The worked reference demonstrates the failure: three unattributed aggregators in one `source` field.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried three refutations. (a) 'Is confidence enough?' — No: reliability and provenance are orthogonal, and a single scalar per fact cannot carry a source that is authoritative on one axis and shaped on another. (b) 'Would a competent execution fix it?' — Partially: a disciplined researcher COULD write 'vendor advisory (Acme PSIRT, 2026-03-04)' into the free string. But nothing requires it, nothing validates it, the board renders it verbatim as an unclassed blob (CardTile.tsx:120-122), and the committed reference — the artifact env.md points at as 'what it worked looks like' — does not do it. So present-broken, not confirmed-absent. (c) 'Is this my topic being hard?' — No: any domain with adversarial or interested sources hits this, which is most of geopolitics and all of fraud.
findings.l2_priority: On a real run, count how many `source` strings name a single retrievable document versus an aggregator list. The reference scored badly; confirm whether that is the researcher or the field.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: The `unhinged` rung IS the motive tier; the mandatory falsifier does not constrain attribution, and no field marks a conclusion that names a living person, company or state
findings.expected: A methodic used on topics with identifiable humans should make attribution HARD rather than available: a leap ladder whose top rung either forbids naming a party as the agent of an act, or demands a falsifier reachable from published material — the same standard `facts[]` already holds itself to.
findings.got: The top rung is specified AS the motive tier: conclusions.ts:32-33 defines `unhinged` as 'A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is — nobody can source what someone intended. Entertaining, defensible as speculation.' The reference implementation ships one against a named living head of state (conclusions.ts:164-179, `leap:"unhinged"` at :169, `hottest:true` at :178) imputing a corrupt purpose. The falsifier requirement is real and structurally mandatory (`falsifiableBy: string`, non-optional, :50) but does not bind: (a) the tier demands a falsifier for a claim class it has itself defined as unsourceable, and the reference resolves the contradiction by substituting a DIFFERENT claim's falsifier — the claim is 'was never meant to be built' (intent), the falsifier is 'a funded, audited reserve with a published coin count' (a fact), and a reserve built late under pressure falsifies the fact while leaving the intent claim untouched; (b) nothing in the `Conclusion` type records that a claim names a person, company or state, so the 😈 badge (CardTile.tsx:61-67, :96) warns about EPISTEMICS ('speculation about motive — not reporting') where a legal warning is what is needed; (c) `far` — 'a genuine reach' (:31) — has ample room to attribute and carries no badge at all, so capping only the top rung disciplines the claims that already announced themselves.
findings.refuter_pass: The brief asked me to contradict it if the falsifier requirement already constrains adequately, and I checked hard before ruling. What IS present and working: the falsifier is type-mandatory (will not compile without one), the header doctrine is explicit ('a synthesis that cannot be wrong is not a conclusion, it is a vibe', :17-19), `hottest` is held to a HIGHER bar not a lower one (:53-58), the UI marks it, and conclusions are opt-in so no attribution reaches a script without a human act (conclusions.ts:15-16, cards.ts:73). This is a designer who saw the hazard and it materially lowers the severity of the realistic failure. It still does not constrain, for the three reasons in `got`, of which (a) is checkable against the committed reference and (c) is the one that would actually bite. Also tested: 'is this my domain being unusually exposed?' — No. The defect is in the TYPE, not in my material, and would read identically to anyone naming a company, a regulator or an individual. That domain-independence is what would make convergence with another area's finding a real signal rather than two people sharing a preference.
findings.content_or_lens_note: Filed content: the shared mechanism CAN hold a required `names: 'none'|'org'|'living-person'|'state'` field plus a rule that anything above 'none' needs a falsifier checkable in published material. One sub-item — a per-domain MAXIMUM leap — is genuinely lens-shaped, because a cap value is a per-domain constant and nothing else; that sub-item alone is `undecided`. I have read the lens bar at SKILL.md:200-206 and am not claiming this finding clears it.
findings.l2_priority: Ask a live run for a conclusion on a topic whose actors are named humans, and check whether the produced falsifier tests the CLAIM or a neighbouring fact. That substitution is the whole mechanism and it is only visible on real output.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: Two facts cannot be linked as contradictory, and the wound graph models support only — so descoping one of a conflicting pair silently resolves the conflict with no warning
findings.expected: Where two published accounts give different dates for the same event, both should live in `facts[]` as dated, sourced cards LINKED as mutually exclusive — and the dependency graph, whose stated job is to warn that cutting a card breaks something, should treat cutting one of a conflicting pair as consequential.
findings.got: `Fact` has no `contradicts`/`conflictsWith` field (types.ts:16-26). `Card.dependsOn` is documented as 'Ids this card needs in order to stand. Descoping any of them wounds it' (cards.ts:25) and is built only from a reversal's evidence and mechanism (cards.ts:59-65) — support only, no representation of mutual exclusion. Consequence: a reviewer descopes one of a conflicting pair, the wound arithmetic reports nothing, and the notebook silently adopts the survivor's timeline. A safety graph blind to the one relation that matters here is worse than no graph, because it produces confidence.
findings.refuter_pass: (a) 'Is the missing thing present somewhere I did not read?' — I checked `counter_positions_to_state_fairly[]` (types.ts:113), which is a bare string[] and can hold the conflict as unsourced prose; and `unknowns[]`, covered separately as SB-04. Neither is a link between two evidence cards. (b) 'Would competent execution produce it anyway?' — A researcher can write both facts today, so the material survives; what cannot be executed into existence is the LINK and the wound behaviour, which are code. (c) 'Is this my topic?' — Conflicting published records are common in geopolitics, fraud and breaking news, so reachability is med rather than low, but I am not claiming high.
findings.l2_priority: Produce a notebook containing a real published-record conflict, then descope one side on the board and record whether anything warns.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: `unknowns[]` — the designated home for source conflict — frames it as a research gap and instructs suppression, and carries no source, date or confidence
findings.expected: A disagreement between two published records is a fact ABOUT THE SOURCES, and in an organisational post-mortem it is frequently the load-bearing one. It should be recordable as evidence, with both citations intact, and the script should be told to PRESENT the conflict rather than avoid the contested value.
findings.got: `Unknown` is defined as 'Something the research could not settle' (types.ts:60) and its `impact` field 'tells the script what it may NOT say' (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:76-78). Both framings are negative — a conflict filed here is recorded as the researcher's failure. The worked precedent confirms the pattern: `u-spot-price` (unknowns.ts:21-26) records that three sources disagree on a price and its impact is 'Never a precise figure' — suppress the contested value. Correct craft for a price; for an incident chronology it deletes the finding. `Unknown` also has no `source`, no `asOf` and no `confidence` (types.ts:68-78), so filing a timeline conflict there loses which document gave which date — the conflict survives as a rumour of a conflict.
findings.refuter_pass: The strongest refutation is real and I am recording it rather than burying it: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:102 gives exactly the right instruction — 'Two datasets that appear to contradict → present as competing readings, never pick silently.' The PROMPT is on my side. So this is not 'the methodic never thought about it'; it is that the schema gives that instruction nowhere to land, and the field the same Phase points at pulls the other way, with a worked example that suppresses. Downgraded from blocker to major on that basis, since a careful researcher reading Phase 7 could route to facts[] instead — which then hits SB-03.
findings.l2_priority: Check where a live run actually files a source conflict — unknowns or facts — and whether the rendered script states the conflict or avoids the contested value.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: The board imports the prompt's domain table while dropping the prompt's own 'for a market/economics topic' scoping
findings.expected: Either a second domain table for non-market topics, or an instruction for deriving one — since the prompt already says its table is the minimum FOR A PARTICULAR KIND OF TOPIC.
findings.got: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:21-22 is scoped and honest: 'Run 4–8 searches covering the subject's distinct causal domains. For a market/economics topic, that is at minimum:'. dimensions.ts:1-5 imports that table as the board's seven fixed columns and its comment NAMES the scoping while discarding it — 'Taken from RESEARCH-PROMPT.md Phase 1, which already defines the causal domains a market/economics run must cover — so the review columns are the research brief's own checklist, not a fresh invention.' A qualified example became an unqualified schema in one import, and the file documents the moment. The prompt offers no alternative table and no derivation rule for a topic that is not a market.
findings.refuter_pass: The obvious refutation is my own column score: 7/7 used, so the market table did NOT fail me and I must not inflate this into a collapse. Holding to that — the finding is not 'the columns do not fit', it is 'the scoping was silently dropped', which is a defect regardless of whether any given topic happens to survive it. Reachability is high because every non-market topic in the cast passes through this import. Filed content, not lens: a second table of rows is content by the SKILL's own definition (SKILL.md:189-199 lists search-domains and dimensions as lens CONTENT, and content is fixable by editing rows).
findings.l2_priority: Record whether a live non-market run invents its own domains at Phase 1 or forces its material into the market six.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: No column and no card kind holds a chronology; the incident timeline lands in 'The number'
findings.expected: For incident anatomy the sequence — compromise, publish, first install, detection, disclosure, patch, advisory — is the primary object, not an attribute of one. It needs a column, and the material for it is the topic's spine.
findings.got: No DIMENSION is time-shaped. `the-number` is magnitude over a window ('What the price actually did, and over what window', dimensions.ts:26-27), which is a quantity, not a sequence. Chronology cards therefore have no correct tag, reach `?? DEFAULT_DIMENSION` (dimensions.ts:62, cards.ts:48) and file under the price column, where a reviewer looking for a sequence will never look.
findings.refuter_pass: (a) 'Is this G-000 re-raised?' — No, and I checked the accepted-gaps entry before filing. G-000 is about cards that HAVE a correct column and were not tagged by a follow-up. Mine have no correct column to be tagged with. Different cause, same landing site; I cite G-000 for the fallback behaviour and claim only the taxonomy half. (b) 'Could mechanisms carry it?' — mechanisms[].chain carries CAUSATION well and could hold a causal sequence, but a chronology's value here is partly non-causal (who knew what when), and a mechanism is not a column. (c) 'Is this my topic being hard?' — Partly yes, which is why frequency is med not high; a market topic genuinely does not need a timeline column.
findings.l2_priority: Check where a live incident run's chronology facts actually land on the board.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: `actors.emptyMeans` asserts an empty column means 'the story has no agents' — for an ownership-gap topic that absence IS the finding
findings.expected: An `emptyMeans` is a claim about what an empty column signifies, and the env file says to test it. For a topic whose thesis is that nobody owned the check, the diagnosis and the defect must not look identical on the board.
findings.got: dimensions.ts:30-31 — `emptyMeans: 'Nobody is named — the story has no agents.'` My story's agent is that there wasn't one. A correctly diagnosed organisational failure and an under-researched notebook therefore produce a similar-looking `actors` column, and the mechanism cannot say which.
findings.refuter_pass: Downgraded from major to minor on the refuter pass, and the reason matters. `actors` DOES hold teams and their governing policy — 'Entities large enough to move this, and what governs their behaviour' describes an internal team and its ownership policy accurately, which contradicts a strict reading of the brief. And `mechanisms[].chain` expresses the gap cleanly: 'Team A ships · THEREFORE Team B assumes the check ran · BUT nobody owns asserting it · THEREFORE the check never runs.' So the MATERIAL is representable and this is a mis-description in one string, not a hole. Minor, and honestly reported as minor.
findings.l2_priority: Low. Confirm only that a produced org-failure notebook has a populated actors column.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: The engine catalogue carries no exposure note; Engine B's move is 'a mechanism a viewer could operate', which for an attack chain is a how-to
findings.expected: An engine whose pleasure depends on the viewer operating the mechanism should carry a caution for subjects where operating it is the hazard. The catalogue already knows how to carry a per-engine caution — ENGINES.md:104-112 is a long, careful note on an Adjudication exemplar whose execution must not be copied — so the file has the shape and simply has not considered the case where the SUBJECT is the hazard rather than the source.
findings.got: ENGINES.md:44-54 recommends Engine B for 'a mechanism a viewer could operate, especially a strange or punishing one', and the choosing table (:162-171) routes 'a mechanism someone could operate' straight to it with no qualification. My topic is a textbook fit — one phished maintainer token against thousands of poisoned builds is the disproportion — and running it as written publishes a tutorial. Nothing in the catalogue, the prompt or the schema flags it.
findings.refuter_pass: (a) 'Is this the methodic or my topic?' — Genuinely partly my topic, hence frequency low; most subjects have no operable hazard. But trust_erosion is high because the failure is a published how-to, and reachability is med because malware, fraud mechanics and several security topics all route here. (b) 'Is it present elsewhere?' — I checked the prompt and the schema for any exposure or safety field and found none; the closest is the ENGINES D-honest note, which is about SOURCE honesty, not subject hazard. (c) 'Would a competent execution catch it?' — A competent human would, which is exactly the argument for writing it down: the catalogue exists so the generator does not depend on the operator's judgement.
findings.l2_priority: If a live run recommends Engine B for an attack chain, record whether the produced script includes operable detail.

findings.creator: security-breach
findings.title: The four-rung evidence ladder with per-rung REQUIREMENTS exists in `knowledge/README.md` and is not wired to `facts[]`
findings.expected: The rung that matters most for advisory handling is OBSERVED, whose requirement is '`source · [mm:ss]` + the quoted line' — a rung that demands the quoted line is the direct antidote to paraphrasing a vendor into authority, which is this field's standing error. Notebook facts should inherit those per-rung requirements.
findings.got: Two unconnected evidence systems in one repo. knowledge/README.md:36-41 defines MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED with a REQUIRES column, governing the knowledge library's own craft claims. Notebook facts use an unqualified `confidence: high|medium|low` (types.ts:12, :21-23) with an optional free-prose `confidenceNote`. Nothing carries the requirement across.
findings.refuter_pass: Deliberately filed MINOR, against my own interest, because the refuter pass largely defeated the stronger version. The brief hypothesised there is no honest rung for interpretive or practitioner-consensus evidence; there is — `confidence:'medium'` plus a stated `confidenceNote`, used exactly that way in the reference at facts.ts:19 ('mechanism reported by one analyst'). That labels my single-source organisational claim without demoting it, so the floor does not bite me and the hypothesis does not survive my topic. What remains is an upgrade opportunity, not a defect: the better instrument exists one file over and is not connected. artifact_check is present-but-missed, which per rubric.md:113 makes this a discoverability finding against `knowledge`, not a gap.
findings.l2_priority: Low. Note whether a live run's confidenceNotes name the document class unprompted.

pre_recorded_not_re_raised: G-000 — untagged cards fall through `?? DEFAULT_DIMENSION` into 'The number' (dimensions.ts:42-49). Cited as the landing mechanism inside G-L1SW-SB-06; the taxonomy cause is distinct and is what SB-06 claims.
known-blocker — L3 has no notebook loader.
scope-note — the app cannot run research; every time-saved number is an estimate of the methodic as written.
by-design — conclusions have no sources; the falsifier substitutes. This is why G-L1SW-SB-02 indicts the falsifier's checkability rather than the missing citation.
